metadata.title: Regorafenib Monotherapy
metadata.indication: Previously treated metastatic colorectal cancer or unresectable/metastatic GIST; 160 mg daily days 1–21 every 28 days.
metadata.partial_assessment_note: Any independently actionable entered value is assessed; omitted domains remain unassessed and do not block a partial result.
metadata.partial_assessment_policy: Each entered value is assessed independently. Omitted domains remain unassessed and are never assumed normal.

catalogue_reconciliation.scope_note: The NCCP states that its website list is not comprehensive. This reconciliation does not assert that every possible national regimen is published online.

encoding_maturity.label: Source reconciled · independent clinical and pharmacy review pending
encoding_maturity.scope_note: Current source-to-rule reconciliation and engine boundary cases in validation/colorectal-v08434/oral-source-audit. Retained source ambiguities and manually assessed domains are explicit. Independent clinical and pharmacy validation remains pending.

metadata.catalogue_source_check_scope: Catalogue presence and source link structure only; not rule level source fidelity.
metadata.source_retrieval_method: Current official HSE PDF retrieved with curl; dose tables visually checked; current EMA supplement archived

source_supplements.label: EMA product information, current retrieved copy
source_supplements.basis: Explicit supplement where NCCP refers to the SmPC; no inferred NCCP threshold

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: The treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Any dose modification should be discussed with a Consultant.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: JSON assessment encoding derived from NCCP 00244 Version 5. Confirm the current official NCCP PDF and use independent clinical judgement. Clinical and oncology-pharmacy validation remain pending.

indications.description: Unresectable or metastatic GIST after imatinib and sunitinib.

treatment_phases.label: 28-day oral cycle
treatment_phases.duration: Until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity

administration.note: Reference starting dose only; actual prescription may be lower. Days 22–28 are tablet-free. Take after a light meal containing <30% fat. Swallow whole; same-day missed dose only, never two doses on one day or replacement after vomiting.

output_templates.contraindicated: The entered data trigger a protocol exclusion or contraindication pathway.
output_templates.discontinue: The entered data trigger protocol discontinuation.
output_templates.withhold: Hold treatment and follow the protocol reassessment pathway.
output_templates.consultant_review: Consultant review is required before treatment proceeds.
output_templates.dose_reduce: Treatment may proceed only after the encoded component modifications are reviewed and prescribed.
output_templates.proceed: No encoded dose-modification criterion was triggered by the entered data.

rule_engine.conflict_policy: Use the most restrictive overall action; combine component changes using the greatest reduction per component rather than summing reductions.
rule_engine.missing_data_policy: Do not infer missing values, recovery, recurrence, current dose, reduction history or clinical context. Entered independent stop/hold findings remain actionable. No automatic patient-specific dose is calculated from a reference dose.

action.recommendation: Do not administer under this NCCP regimen; resolve the hypersensitivity to regorafenib or an excipient exclusion with the treating consultant.

rules.explanation: Do not administer under this NCCP regimen; resolve the hypersensitivity to regorafenib or an excipient exclusion with the treating consultant.

rules.explanation: Do not administer under this NCCP regimen; resolve the recent myocardial infarction (smpc studies excluded within 6 months) exclusion with the treating consultant.

rules.explanation: Do not administer under this NCCP regimen; resolve the cardiac failure exclusion with the treating consultant.

action.recommendation: Same-class hypersensitivity requires consultant assessment; distinguish this caution from regorafenib/excipient hypersensitivity.

rules.explanation: Same-class hypersensitivity requires consultant assessment; distinguish this caution from regorafenib/excipient hypersensitivity.

action.recommendation: NCCP eligibility is ECOG 0–1; ECOG >1 requires individual consultant review.

rules.explanation: NCCP eligibility is ECOG 0–1; ECOG >1 requires individual consultant review.

action.recommendation: Adequate marrow, renal and hepatic function is required. NCCP does not give numeric entry thresholds; do not substitute another regimen's thresholds.

rules.explanation: Adequate marrow, renal and hepatic function is required. NCCP does not give numeric entry thresholds; do not substitute another regimen's thresholds.

action.recommendation: Confirm CRC prior treatment/suitability (fluoropyrimidine, anti-VEGF and anti-EGFR) or GIST progression/intolerance after imatinib and sunitinib before treatment.

rules.explanation: Confirm CRC prior treatment/suitability (fluoropyrimidine, anti-VEGF and anti-EGFR) or GIST progression/intolerance after imatinib and sunitinib before treatment.

action.recommendation: This NCCP regimen covers colorectal cancer and GIST; another indication needs its own source and consultant plan.

rules.explanation: This NCCP regimen covers colorectal cancer and GIST; another indication needs its own source and consultant plan.

action.recommendation: Severe hepatic impairment / Child-Pugh C: regorafenib is not recommended.

rules.explanation: Severe hepatic impairment / Child-Pugh C: regorafenib is not recommended.

action.recommendation: Child-Pugh A: no dose adjustment needed. For B, NCCP Table 1 expects no adjustment, but current EMA section 4.2 provides no dose recommendation because data are limited. Resolve this source difference with the consultant and monitor closely; no automatic dose or clearance.

source.section: Table 1; current EMA section 4.2 p4 differs for B

rules.explanation: Child-Pugh A: no dose adjustment needed. For B, NCCP Table 1 expects no adjustment, but current EMA section 4.2 provides no dose recommendation because data are limited. Resolve this source difference with the consultant and monitor closely; no automatic dose or clearance.

action.recommendation: NCCP Table 1 expects no dose adjustment with haemodialysis; agree an individual specialist plan. Do not borrow a renal dose reduction or issue automatic clearance.

rules.explanation: NCCP Table 1 expects no dose adjustment with haemodialysis; agree an individual specialist plan. Do not borrow a renal dose reduction or issue automatic clearance.

action.recommendation: Prescribed regorafenib dose is outside the NCCP 80–160 mg/day range; reconcile before administration.

rules.explanation: Prescribed regorafenib dose is outside the NCCP 80–160 mg/day range; reconcile before administration.

action.recommendation: A 40 mg decrement must be based on the actual current dose and prior reductions, not the 160 mg reference dose. Confirm both before prescribing.

rules.explanation: A 40 mg decrement must be based on the actual current dose and prior reductions, not the 160 mg reference dose. Confirm both before prescribing.

action.recommendation: A further 40 mg decrease would breach the minimum 80 mg/day. Do not prescribe below the source floor; seek consultant discontinuation/alternative-plan review. Previous reduction count alone cannot select a dose after any re-escalation.

rules.explanation: A further 40 mg decrease would breach the minimum 80 mg/day. Do not prescribe below the source floor; seek consultant discontinuation/alternative-plan review. Previous reduction count alone cannot select a dose after any re-escalation.

action.recommendation: Regorafenib uses 40 mg tablet steps: reconcile a prescribed daily dose other than 80, 120 or 160 mg before administration.

rules.explanation: Regorafenib uses 40 mg tablet steps: reconcile a prescribed daily dose other than 80, 120 or 160 mg before administration.

action.recommendation: Do not restart automatically. The source-specific recovery, interruption duration, current dose and benefit/risk decision must be confirmed by the treating consultant.

rules.explanation: Do not restart automatically. The source-specific recovery, interruption duration, current dose and benefit/risk decision must be confirmed by the treating consultant.

action.recommendation: Regorafenib re-escalation is discretionary and condition-specific, not automatic. Hypertension must be controlled for at least one full cycle; HFSR/other-toxicity pathways have their own conditions. Confirm the consultant plan.

rules.explanation: Regorafenib re-escalation is discretionary and condition-specific, not automatic. Hypertension must be controlled for at least one full cycle; HFSR/other-toxicity pathways have their own conditions. Confirm the consultant plan.

action.recommendation: Grade 1 HFSR: maintain the current dose for this domain and institute immediate supportive measures; other domains remain unassessed.

rules.explanation: Grade 1 HFSR: maintain the current dose for this domain and institute immediate supportive measures; other domains remain unassessed.

action.recommendation: Grade 2 HFSR requires occurrence and 7-day response review. First occurrence uses a 40 mg reduction; persistent/recurrent disease requires interruption. Do not assume first occurrence or recovery.

rules.explanation: Grade 2 HFSR requires occurrence and 7-day response review. First occurrence uses a 40 mg reduction; persistent/recurrent disease requires interruption. Do not assume first occurrence or recovery.

action.recommendation: First grade 2 HFSR: reduce the current dose by 40 mg and institute supportive measures; minimum 80 mg/day. If improvement fails despite reduction, interrupt for at least 7 days until grade 0–1. Do not apply a second reduction to the same episode automatically.

rules.explanation: First grade 2 HFSR: reduce the current dose by 40 mg and institute supportive measures; minimum 80 mg/day. If improvement fails despite reduction, interrupt for at least 7 days until grade 0–1. Do not apply a second reduction to the same episode automatically.

action.recommendation: Confirm whether the 40 mg reduction has already been applied for this episode before recommending another reduction; missing history is not a first untreated episode.

rules.explanation: Confirm whether the 40 mg reduction has already been applied for this episode before recommending another reduction; missing history is not a first untreated episode.

action.recommendation: Interrupt until HFSR grade 0–1; when authorised, restart 40 mg below the actual prior dose (floor 80 mg). After failure of the initial reduction, interruption is at least 7 days. Confirm occurrence and reduction history.

rules.explanation: Interrupt until HFSR grade 0–1; when authorised, restart 40 mg below the actual prior dose (floor 80 mg). After failure of the initial reduction, interruption is at least 7 days. Confirm occurrence and reduction history.

action.recommendation: Fourth grade 2 HFSR occurrence: permanently discontinue regorafenib.

rules.explanation: Fourth grade 2 HFSR occurrence: permanently discontinue regorafenib.

action.recommendation: Grade 3 HFSR independently requires interruption for at least 7 days and until grade 0–1; do not wait for occurrence history to hold. Third occurrence requires permanent discontinuation.

rules.explanation: Grade 3 HFSR independently requires interruption for at least 7 days and until grade 0–1; do not wait for occurrence history to hold. Third occurrence requires permanent discontinuation.

action.recommendation: First/second grade 3 HFSR: supportive care, interrupt for at least 7 days AND until grade 0–1; then consultant-authorised restart 40 mg lower, minimum 80 mg/day.

rules.explanation: First/second grade 3 HFSR: supportive care, interrupt for at least 7 days AND until grade 0–1; then consultant-authorised restart 40 mg lower, minimum 80 mg/day.

action.recommendation: Third grade 3 HFSR occurrence: permanently discontinue.

rules.explanation: Third grade 3 HFSR occurrence: permanently discontinue.

action.recommendation: HFSR has not recovered to grade 0–1; do not restart.

rules.explanation: HFSR has not recovered to grade 0–1; do not restart.

action.recommendation: The source-required minimum seven-day HFSR interruption is not documented as completed. Recovery alone does not waive that minimum.

rules.explanation: The source-required minimum seven-day HFSR interruption is not documented as completed. Recovery alone does not waive that minimum.

action.recommendation: ALT/AST ≤5 × ULN alone permits continuation in Table 3. If elevated, monitor liver function weekly until <3 × ULN or baseline. Check concurrent bilirubin and previous toxicity; this is not global clearance.

rules.explanation: ALT/AST ≤5 × ULN alone permits continuation in Table 3. If elevated, monitor liver function weekly until <3 × ULN or baseline. Check concurrent bilirubin and previous toxicity; this is not global clearance.

action.recommendation: ALT/AST >5 to ≤20 × ULN: interrupt independently of missing recurrence history; monitor weekly until <3 × ULN or baseline. Recurrence requires permanent discontinuation.

rules.explanation: ALT/AST >5 to ≤20 × ULN: interrupt independently of missing recurrence history; monitor weekly until <3 × ULN or baseline. Recurrence requires permanent discontinuation.

action.recommendation: First ALT/AST >5 to ≤20 × ULN: interrupt until <3 × ULN or baseline. Only if benefit outweighs risk may the consultant restart 40 mg lower (minimum 80 mg), with weekly liver tests for at least 4 weeks.

rules.explanation: First ALT/AST >5 to ≤20 × ULN: interrupt until <3 × ULN or baseline. Only if benefit outweighs risk may the consultant restart 40 mg lower (minimum 80 mg), with weekly liver tests for at least 4 weeks.

action.recommendation: Recurrent ALT/AST >5 × ULN: permanently discontinue.

rules.explanation: Recurrent ALT/AST >5 × ULN: permanently discontinue.

action.recommendation: ALT/AST >20 × ULN at any occurrence: permanently discontinue.

rules.explanation: ALT/AST >20 × ULN at any occurrence: permanently discontinue.

action.recommendation: ALT/AST >3 × ULN with concurrent bilirubin >2 × ULN, without the confirmed Gilbert’s exception: permanently discontinue; weekly liver tests until resolution/baseline.

rules.explanation: ALT/AST >3 × ULN with concurrent bilirubin >2 × ULN, without the confirmed Gilbert’s exception: permanently discontinue; weekly liver tests until resolution/baseline.

action.recommendation: Do not administer: combined ALT/AST >3 and bilirubin >2 × ULN normally requires permanent discontinuation. Confirm whether the specific Gilbert’s exception applies; do not infer it from the bilirubin value.

rules.explanation: Do not administer: combined ALT/AST >3 and bilirubin >2 × ULN normally requires permanent discontinuation. Confirm whether the specific Gilbert’s exception applies; do not infer it from the bilirubin value.

action.recommendation: Confirmed Gilbert’s syndrome: use the ALT/AST-specific Table 3 pathway rather than the combined-bilirubin automatic stop. Confirm causation and monitor; higher transaminase/recurrence stops still apply.

rules.explanation: Confirmed Gilbert’s syndrome: use the ALT/AST-specific Table 3 pathway rather than the combined-bilirubin automatic stop. Confirm causation and monitor; higher transaminase/recurrence stops still apply.

action.recommendation: After liver injury, do not restart before transaminases are <3 × ULN or baseline.

rules.explanation: After liver injury, do not restart before transaminases are <3 × ULN or baseline.

action.recommendation: Biochemical recovery alone does not authorise liver-event restart; consultant benefit/risk approval and a 40 mg reduction are required.

rules.explanation: Biochemical recovery alone does not authorise liver-event restart; consultant benefit/risk approval and a 40 mg reduction are required.

action.recommendation: Control blood pressure before initiating regorafenib.

rules.explanation: Control blood pressure before initiating regorafenib.

action.recommendation: Grade 1 hypertension: consider increasing the frequency of blood-pressure monitoring.

rules.explanation: Grade 1 hypertension: consider increasing the frequency of blood-pressure monitoring.

action.recommendation: Confirmed asymptomatic grade 2: initiate/adjust antihypertensive therapy; continuation may be appropriate. If DBP remains >100 mmHg despite new therapy, reduce one level. The source prints >200 mmHg in one diastolic-rise criterion; treat that text as unresolved and verify clinical grading, not a calculated threshold.

rules.explanation: Confirmed asymptomatic grade 2: initiate/adjust antihypertensive therapy; continuation may be appropriate. If DBP remains >100 mmHg despite new therapy, reduce one level. The source prints >200 mmHg in one diastolic-rise criterion; treat that text as unresolved and verify clinical grading, not a calculated threshold.

action.recommendation: Symptomatic grade 2: hold until symptoms resolve AND diastolic BP ≤100 mmHg; treat hypertension. If DBP is not controlled with new therapy, reduce one 40 mg level.

rules.explanation: Symptomatic grade 2: hold until symptoms resolve AND diastolic BP ≤100 mmHg; treat hypertension. If DBP is not controlled with new therapy, reduce one 40 mg level.

action.recommendation: Grade 3: hold until symptoms resolve AND DBP ≤100 mmHg; intensify antihypertensives. Restart at one 40 mg level lower; if not controlled despite more intensive therapy another reduction may be required. Do not reduce below 80 mg.

rules.explanation: Grade 3: hold until symptoms resolve AND DBP ≤100 mmHg; intensify antihypertensives. Restart at one 40 mg level lower; if not controlled despite more intensive therapy another reduction may be required. Do not reduce below 80 mg.

action.recommendation: Grade 4 hypertension / hypertensive crisis: discontinue regorafenib.

rules.explanation: Grade 4 hypertension / hypertensive crisis: discontinue regorafenib.

action.recommendation: The supplied blood pressure meets the NCCP Table 4 grade 3 numeric range (SBP ≥160 or DBP ≥100). Hold and confirm symptoms, grade, antihypertensive treatment and restart plan. DBP exactly 100 is also in the recovery wording: it never authorises restart by itself.

rules.explanation: The supplied blood pressure meets the NCCP Table 4 grade 3 numeric range (SBP ≥160 or DBP ≥100). Hold and confirm symptoms, grade, antihypertensive treatment and restart plan. DBP exactly 100 is also in the recovery wording: it never authorises restart by itself.

action.recommendation: Blood pressure remains uncontrolled despite additional antihypertensive therapy; hold and review a further 40 mg reduction, actual dose history and the 80 mg minimum.

rules.explanation: Blood pressure remains uncontrolled despite additional antihypertensive therapy; hold and review a further 40 mg reduction, actual dose history and the 80 mg minimum.

action.recommendation: Hypertension requiring a delay of more than 4 weeks: go off protocol therapy. A delay for another reason does not satisfy this criterion.

rules.explanation: Hypertension requiring a delay of more than 4 weeks: go off protocol therapy. A delay for another reason does not satisfy this criterion.

action.recommendation: Hypertension requiring a further dose reduction below 80 mg: go off protocol therapy. Confirm actual dose and re-escalation history rather than treating a lifetime reduction count as the current dose.

rules.explanation: Hypertension requiring a further dose reduction below 80 mg: go off protocol therapy. Confirm actual dose and re-escalation history rather than treating a lifetime reduction count as the current dose.

action.recommendation: Hypertension symptoms have not resolved; DBP improvement alone does not permit restart.

rules.explanation: Hypertension symptoms have not resolved; DBP improvement alone does not permit restart.

action.recommendation: Grade 3–4 other toxicity needs urgent source-specific classification before the next dose. Table 5 excludes liver injury, HFSR, hypertension, alopecia, non-refractory nausea/vomiting or hypersensitivity, and asymptomatic laboratory abnormalities; those need their own pathway.

rules.explanation: Grade 3–4 other toxicity needs urgent source-specific classification before the next dose. Table 5 excludes liver injury, HFSR, hypertension, alopecia, non-refractory nausea/vomiting or hypersensitivity, and asymptomatic laboratory abnormalities; those need their own pathway.

action.recommendation: Table 5 grade 3–4 toxicity: delay until grade <2, then consultant-authorised 40 mg reduction from the actual dose (floor 80 mg). Grade 4 may merit permanent discontinuation at consultant discretion. No recovery after a 4-week delay requires permanent discontinuation.

rules.explanation: Table 5 grade 3–4 toxicity: delay until grade <2, then consultant-authorised 40 mg reduction from the actual dose (floor 80 mg). Grade 4 may merit permanent discontinuation at consultant discretion. No recovery after a 4-week delay requires permanent discontinuation.

action.recommendation: Qualifying other toxicity has not recovered to grade <2 after a 4-week delay: permanently discontinue. Confirm that this delay was for the prior Table 5 grade 3–4 event.

rules.explanation: Qualifying other toxicity has not recovered to grade <2 after a 4-week delay: permanently discontinue. Confirm that this delay was for the prior Table 5 grade 3–4 event.

action.recommendation: For a prior Table 5 grade 3–4 event, grade 2 is not recovered: restart requires grade <2.

rules.explanation: For a prior Table 5 grade 3–4 event, grade 2 is not recovered: restart requires grade <2.

action.recommendation: If grade ≥3 other toxicity recurs after re-escalation, institute permanent dose reduction; do not repeat automatic re-escalation.

rules.explanation: If grade ≥3 other toxicity recurs after re-escalation, institute permanent dose reduction; do not repeat automatic re-escalation.

action.recommendation: Urgent clinical assessment; consider treatment interruption for worsening infection. Do not resume until the consultant has assessed recovery.

rules.explanation: Urgent clinical assessment; consider treatment interruption for worsening infection. Do not resume until the consultant has assessed recovery.

action.recommendation: Urgent assessment and hold; permanent discontinuation should be considered for severe bleeding requiring urgent medical intervention.

rules.explanation: Urgent assessment and hold; permanent discontinuation should be considered for severe bleeding requiring urgent medical intervention.

action.recommendation: Discontinue regorafenib for gastrointestinal perforation or fistula and arrange urgent management.

rules.explanation: Discontinue regorafenib for gastrointestinal perforation or fistula and arrange urgent management.

action.recommendation: Interrupt until cardiac ischaemia/infarction resolves. Restart needs individual consultant benefit/risk review; permanently discontinue if it does not resolve.

rules.explanation: Interrupt until cardiac ischaemia/infarction resolves. Restart needs individual consultant benefit/risk review; permanently discontinue if it does not resolve.

action.recommendation: Non-resolving cardiac ischaemia/infarction: permanently discontinue.

rules.explanation: Non-resolving cardiac ischaemia/infarction: permanently discontinue.

action.recommendation: Discontinue for PRES, control hypertension and provide appropriate supportive management.

rules.explanation: Discontinue for PRES, control hypertension and provide appropriate supportive management.

action.recommendation: Urgent management and hold; permanent discontinuation should be considered for confirmed hyperammonaemic encephalopathy.

rules.explanation: Urgent management and hold; permanent discontinuation should be considered for confirmed hyperammonaemic encephalopathy.

action.recommendation: Discontinue regorafenib for TMA and institute prompt treatment.

rules.explanation: Discontinue regorafenib for TMA and institute prompt treatment.

action.recommendation: Interrupt for major surgery; restart only after clinician-confirmed adequate wound healing. This source gives no fixed number of days to substitute.

rules.explanation: Interrupt for major surgery; restart only after clinician-confirmed adequate wound healing. This source gives no fixed number of days to substitute.

action.recommendation: Check electrolytes/thyroid/pancreatic markers as relevant, replace deficits and consider interruption, reduction or discontinuation according to persistence and clinical significance.

rules.explanation: Check electrolytes/thyroid/pancreatic markers as relevant, replace deficits and consider interruption, reduction or discontinuation according to persistence and clinical significance.

action.recommendation: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers and strong UGT1A9 inhibitors; reconcile all prescriptions, OTC/herbal products and grapefruit with oncology pharmacy before administration.

rules.explanation: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers and strong UGT1A9 inhibitors; reconcile all prescriptions, OTC/herbal products and grapefruit with oncology pharmacy before administration.

action.recommendation: Review substrate exposure and toxicity with oncology pharmacy (including irinotecan and rosuvastatin). Do not calculate a regorafenib dose from an interaction flag.

rules.explanation: Review substrate exposure and toxicity with oncology pharmacy (including irinotecan and rosuvastatin). Do not calculate a regorafenib dose from an interaction flag.

action.recommendation: Monitor INR/coagulation and blood counts closely as appropriate; arrange an individual bleeding-risk and interaction plan.

rules.explanation: Monitor INR/coagulation and blood counts closely as appropriate; arrange an individual bleeding-risk and interaction plan.

action.recommendation: Before starting a VEGF-pathway inhibitor, assess aneurysm/dissection risk, including hypertension and a history of aneurysm. No numerical dose reduction is specified.

rules.explanation: Before starting a VEGF-pathway inhibitor, assess aneurysm/dissection risk, including hypertension and a history of aneurysm. No numerical dose reduction is specified.

action.recommendation: Arrange urgent assessment, including ammonia measurement and appropriate clinical management; consider hyperammonaemic encephalopathy, PRES and other causes. Do not infer a definitive diagnosis from this symptom flag.

rules.explanation: Arrange urgent assessment, including ammonia measurement and appropriate clinical management; consider hyperammonaemic encephalopathy, PRES and other causes. Do not infer a definitive diagnosis from this symptom flag.

action.recommendation: Verify 160 mg reference schedule days 1–21 every 28 days and actual prescribed dose. Take after a light meal (<30% fat) at the same time; swallow whole. A missed dose can be taken that same day; no double dose or replacement after vomiting.

rules.explanation: Verify 160 mg reference schedule days 1–21 every 28 days and actual prescribed dose. Take after a light meal (<30% fat) at the same time; swallow whole. A missed dose can be taken that same day; no double dose or replacement after vomiting.

supportive_care.mapping_basis: Oral SACT classification from NCCP V6 Table 8.
supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for oral SACT
notes: NCCP p6: oral minimal-to-low emetogenic risk; no usual premedication. Use a local breakthrough plan.
Prevent/manage HFSR promptly with local skin/foot care.

Baseline: FBC, renal/liver, TFT, BP; lipase/amylase if indicated and ECG/QT if at risk. LFT every 2 weeks for 2 months then monthly; BP weekly for 6 weeks then each cycle. Regular FBC/renal; TFT/lipase/amylase as indicated; INR closely with warfarin.
NCCP p1 meal wording conflicts; current EMA confirms after a light meal <30% fat. Contraception during treatment and 8 weeks after per EMA 4.6.
